title: 13 Nov 2026

topics.news: CAG audits discoms first (FY21–FY26), then transmission, generation, renewables, RDSS. Private discoms are outside scope.

blocks.h: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

rows: Independent constitutional authority that audits the accounts of the Union and States; guardian of the public purse
**Art. 148** (appointment, oath, service conditions), **149** (duties and powers), **150** (form of accounts, prescribed by the President on CAG advice), **151** (audit reports)
**President**, by warrant under hand and seal
**6 years or age 65**, whichever is earlier
Same manner and grounds as a **Supreme Court judge**: President's order after an **address by both Houses** (special majority) on proved misbehaviour or incapacity

Salary and service conditions like an SC judge, set by Parliament, cannot be varied to the holder's disadvantage during term; **barred from any further office** under the Union or a State after retirement; expenses charged on the **Consolidated Fund**
**CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971**
**Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account**, government companies, corporations, bodies substantially financed by government
To the **President** (Union) / **Governor** (State), laid before **Parliament / State Legislature**; examined by the **Public Accounts Committee (PAC)**
CAG is called the "friend, philosopher and guide" of the PAC
CAG appoints the statutory auditor and conducts supplementary audit under the **Companies Act, 2013**
Does not audit purely private companies; no direct power to enforce; works through Parliament

ul: **Controller General of Accounts** (Finance Ministry): keeps accounts; audit and accounts were separated in 1976.
**Parliamentary committees:** PAC, Estimates Committee, Committee on Public Undertakings.
**Other independent constitutional offices:** Election Commission (Art. 324), UPSC (Art. 315), Finance Commission (Art. 280), Attorney General (Art. 76), National Commissions for SC/ST.
**Anti-corruption bodies:** Central Vigilance Commission (statutory), Lokpal, CBI.
**International:** INTOSAI — the global body of Supreme Audit Institutions; India's CAG is an active member.
**Foreign counterparts:** the US Government Accountability Office, the UK National Audit Office.
Discoms are state-owned distribution companies (a few are private); they supply at tariffs below cost and have high **AT&C losses**.
Earlier fixes: **UDAY (2015)**; now **RDSS (2021)**. A CAG audit found UDAY missed its goals.
**Electricity Act, 2003** is the framework; **Electricity is on the Concurrent List** (Entry 38).

topics.mains: CAG's independence and reach (private discoms excluded); audit findings only matter if Parliament acts on them.

topics.news: op-ed says the 2025-26 Special Intensive Revision is a technology failure: central ERONet platform, "logical discrepancy" flags, name-matching errors, Form 6 mismatch, unpublished hearing rules.

rows: Permanent constitutional body for **elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President**; **Art. 324**
Chief Election Commissioner + other Election Commissioners, fixed by the President
**Act of 2023**: selection committee of PM, a Union Minister and the Leader of Opposition (after the Supreme Court's 2023 ruling asked for a neutral process)
**CEC** only like a Supreme Court judge (special-majority address by both Houses); other Commissioners removed on the **CEC's recommendation**
**Art. 325** (one general roll, no one excluded on religion, race, caste, sex); **Art. 326** (universal adult suffrage, age **18** after the 61st Amendment, 1988)
**Representation of the People Act, 1950** (rolls, seat allocation, qualifications to register; Section 21 revision of rolls) and **1951** (conduct of elections, disqualification, corrupt practices)
Prepare and update rolls, delimitation (via Delimitation Commission), registration and symbols for parties, model code of conduct, monitor expenditure
Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Booth Level Officer (BLO); **Form 6** (new registration), Form 7 (objection), Form 8 (correction)
**Puttaswamy (2017)** protected privacy; Aadhaar linkage is voluntary for the roll
Court did not stay it and suggested Aadhaar, EPIC and ration card be accepted; ECI said Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship. A Supreme Court verdict upholding the SIR (May 2026) has been reported.

items.p: **Similar bodies:** State Election Commissions, Delimitation Commission, UPSC, Finance Commission (all independent bodies with security of tenure).

topics.mains: accuracy vs inclusion; the burden of proof on the voter; need for pilots, change freeze, written SOPs.

topics.t: LADAKH polls and the Sixth Schedule
topics.news: panchayat/municipal polls on 21 Nov, hill council polls on 4 Dec; Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance want a delay; talks on statehood and Sixth Schedule stalled; Centre floated a special model under Art. 371.

blocks.h: Fifth and Sixth Schedules, Art. 371, UTs

rows: Administration and control of **Scheduled Areas** and Scheduled Tribes in all States **except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**; Governor's report, **Tribes Advisory Council**, power to regulate land transfer
Tribal areas of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**; **Autonomous District Councils (ADC)** and Regional Councils

Elected members plus a few nominated by the Governor; **5-year term**; makes laws on land (not reserved forest), shifting cultivation, village administration, inheritance, marriage, social customs; courts and tax powers; Governor can dissolve
**Art. 371 to 371J** give special arrangements to Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh/Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Karnataka
**Art. 239–241**; Ladakh is a UT **without a legislature** (J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019)
**73rd/74th Amendments** (Part IX, IXA); **PESA 1996** extends panchayats to Scheduled Areas
Hill Development Councils for Leh and Kargil; now six districts with their own councils
Sixth Schedule would need a constitutional amendment; NCST recommended inclusion in 2021

items.p: **People and geography:** over 90% of Ladakh's population is Scheduled Tribe; **Balti** (Kargil), **Brokpa** (Dha-Hanu), **Changpa** (nomads, **pashmina** goats, Changthang plateau). Cold desert, high passes close in winter.
**Related bodies:** National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Art. 338A), Tribal Affairs Ministry, Governor's Tribes Advisory Council.

topics.mains: why tribal land, culture and jobs need constitutional safeguards; consultation before scheduling polls.

topics.news: OBC groups call a protest on 28 Nov; want a drop-down list and unique caste codes; the Centre chose an open column for all but SC/ST.

rows: Decennial; **Census Act, 1948**; Census is a **Union subject** (Seventh Schedule, Entry 69, List I); conducted by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, Home Ministry
First complete synchronous census **1881**; caste last counted in **1931**; after independence only SC/ST counted
Socio-Economic and Caste Census; caste data never released

**Art. 340** (commission to study backward classes); **Kaka Kalelkar** (1953) and **Mandal Commission** (1979) → 27% OBC reservation (1990); **Indra Sawhney (1992)** upheld it, set the **50% cap** and the **creamy layer**
**Art. 15(4), 16(4)** (special provisions), **Art. 342A** (102nd Amendment: NCBC constitutional body, President lists OBC), 105th Amendment (states can list their own OBC)
A commission under Art. 340 (Rohini) examined splitting the OBC quota

topics.mains: data for targeting benefits vs risks of mis-recording and politicisation; open column vs coded list.

topics.news: Adi community protests the proposed dam (NHPC; only at Pre-Feasibility Report stage); villages to be submerged; consent claimed only for the PFR; China's Medog dam upstream; no water treaty with China.

rows: Gravity, arch, earth/rock-fill; **storage** vs **run-of-river**; "live storage" = usable water
Over 6,000 large dams; third in the world after China and the US; **Maharashtra has the most**
**Highest operating: Tehri** · **largest reservoir: Indira Sagar** · **longest: Hirakud** · **highest under construction: Dibang** · "smallest": no official answer

**State subject** (Entry 17, List II); **inter-State river regulation is Union** (Entry 56, List I); **Art. 262** (disputes); **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956**; **River Boards Act 1956**; **Brahmaputra Board (1980)**
**Central Water Commission**, **NHPC**, **National Dam Safety Authority** under the **Dam Safety Act, 2021**
**EIA Notification 2006** (public hearing, expert appraisal committee); **Forest Conservation Act 1980**; **Forest Rights Act 2006** (gram sabha consent); **LARR Act 2013** (consent, rehabilitation)
**Inner Line Permit** (Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation 1873); **Art. 371H** (Governor's special responsibility); formerly NEFA; statehood 1987

items.p: **Geography:** Yarlung Tsangpo (Tibet) → **Siang** (enters near Gelling) → joins Dibang and Lohit → **Brahmaputra**; the "Missing Link"; Upper Siang has gorges and **Mouling National Park**; eastern Himalaya is seismically active. Arunachal is India's **hydropower frontier** (about 40% of national potential).
**People:** **Adi**; faith **Donyi-Polo**; goddess **Kine Nane**; harvest festival **Solung**. At stake: burial grounds, ancestral land.
**Agriculture:** rice (staple), maize, millets; **jhum** (shifting); valley wet rice yields more; **oranges, ginger, turmeric, banana, pineapple**.

**History of dam opposition:** **Narmada Bachao Andolan** (World Bank withdrew in 1994) · **Tehri** (Sunderlal Bahuguna, built despite protests) · **Silent Valley** (dropped) · Koel-Karo · Lower Subansiri and Dibang.
**International:** Expert Level Mechanism with China (2006); GERD (Ethiopia–Egypt–Sudan); Indus Waters Treaty (see §7).

topics.mains: strategic water security vs consent and ecology; smaller tributary dams; consent for a PFR is not consent for a dam.

topics.t: INDIA–BANGLADESH: Hasina row, Ganga Water Treaty
topics.news: Hasina applied for a passport; Dhaka rejects it and wants her back via extradition; the Ganga treaty expires next month; talks stalled; ties down.

rows: India helped create Bangladesh in **1971**; **Neighbourhood First** policy
**Land Boundary Agreement (2015)** implemented by the **100th Constitution Amendment**; enclaves exchanged; **Tin Bigha corridor**
Many shared rivers; **Joint Rivers Commission (1972)**; **Ganga Water Treaty (12 Dec 1996)**, 30-year term, dry-season sharing at **Farakka**; **Teesta** deal never concluded
Barrage (1975) diverts water to the **Hooghly** to keep **Kolkata port** navigable
**Extradition Act, 1962**; extradition treaty with Bangladesh (2013); **Art. 253** (Parliament legislates to implement treaties); **Art. 51** (promote peace)
**Ganga**: Gangotri → Bhagirathi → Devprayag → plains; **Padma** in Bangladesh; **Petrapole–Benapole** land port

topics.mains: a neighbour's domestic politics and an exiled leader; water treaty renewal as leverage.

topics.t: INDUS WATERS TREATY — Court of Arbitration
topics.news: the Court (31 Aug 2026) held the treaty remains in force and abeyance is unauthorised; India does not recognise it.

ul: **Treaty 1960**, brokered by the **World Bank**; **eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan**, with limited Indian use (run-of-river hydropower, irrigation). **Permanent Indus Commission**; dispute path: questions → differences → **Neutral Expert** or **Court of Arbitration**.
Disputes: **Kishanganga**, **Ratle**, Baglihar.
**Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969)**: treaties cannot be unilaterally suspended; "fundamental change of circumstances" is the usual argument.
**Geography:** Indus rises near **Mansarovar** (Tibet), flows through Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan, then Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. Pakistan's agriculture depends on the Indus system.

topics.mains: water as strategic leverage; legality of "abeyance"; compare with China's upstream dams on the Brahmaputra.

topics.news: FTA concluded earlier in 2026; supply-chain integration, Project 75(I) submarines with TKMS built in India, green partnership, students and skilled workers, Tamil Nadu hub.

ul: **FTA vs CEPA vs PTA:** an FTA removes tariffs on most goods; a CEPA also covers services, investment and cooperation; a PTA reduces tariffs on a limited list. **WTO/GATT** is the multilateral base.

**India–EU:** relations since 1962; **Strategic Partnership 2004**; **Trade and Technology Council (2022)**; FTA talks restarted after a long gap. **CBAM** (EU carbon border tax) is a concern for Indian steel, aluminium and cement.
**Domestic bodies:** Commerce Ministry, **DGFT**, **Foreign Trade Policy**, Make in India.
**Defence:** **Strategic Partnership Model (2017)** for building submarines, fighters and helicopters with foreign partners; **P-75(I)** is the conventional submarine programme.
**Germany:** federal republic of **Länder**; part of **G4** (with India, Japan, Brazil) seeking a UN Security Council seat; **migration and mobility agreement (2022)** for skilled workers.
**Geography:** Tamil Nadu's **Chennai–Oragadam–Hosur** automotive belt, **Coimbatore** for engineering and wind components.

topics.mains: FTA gains vs sector risks; technology transfer in defence; skilled migration.

topics.news: COP31 at Antalya; many leaders absent; finance mechanics deferred; India declined the electrification pledge. Earthshot Prize held in India.

rows: Rio Earth Summit; **Conference of Parties (COP)** meets annually; **common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR)**
Binding targets on developed (Annex I) countries; Clean Development Mechanism
Hold warming well below **2°C**, pursue **1.5°C**; **NDCs** set by each country; 5-year cycles; **Art. 6** (carbon markets), **Art. 9** (developed countries' finance)
Periodic check on progress under Paris; the first concluded at COP28 (Dubai)
**Green Climate Fund**; **Loss and Damage fund** (agreed COP27, operational after COP28); **NCQG (COP29, Baku)** of at least $300 bn a year by 2035, which **India rejected as too little, too late**
UN science body that produces assessment reports

**Net zero by 2070**; Panchamrit (COP26); 500 GW non-fossil by 2030; **LiFE**; **National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008)**; **National Green Hydrogen Mission**; **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**; **Art. 48A and 51A(g)**
**International Solar Alliance** (HQ Gurugram), **Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)**
**Montreal Protocol (1987)**, Kigali Amendment — success model for ozone
Founded 2020 by Prince William; five themes (nature, clean air, oceans, waste-free, climate); Indian finalists: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, **Mahila Housing Trust** (linked to **SEWA**, Ahmedabad)

topics.mains: finance, not targets, is the sticking point; India's CBDR stand.

topics.news: AQI 'severe' after Deepavali; student protests; Section 163 BNSS orders; Yamuna dead-fish spat.

rows: **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**; **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**; **CAQM Act, 2021** (Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR; replaced EPCA)
**Art. 21** (clean air, via M.C. Mehta cases — CNG order for Delhi buses); **Art. 48A, 51A(g)**
National AQI (2014): **Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor, Severe**
Graded Response Action Plan: stage-wise curbs as AQI worsens; CAQM invoked Stage III on 6 Nov 2026 per reports
National Clean Air Programme: city-level PM reduction targets
Vehicles, construction dust, industry, biomass burning; **stubble burning** in Punjab and Haryana adds a share in November; firecrackers on Deepavali
**Temperature inversion** and low wind speed trap pollutants; Delhi lies in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**, with the Himalaya blocking dispersal
Rice–wheat cycle leaves short gap; solutions: **Happy Seeder**, PUSA decomposer, crop diversification
**PM2.5** reaches alveoli; COPD, asthma, children and pregnant women most at risk
Rises at **Yamunotri**; worst-polluted in the Delhi stretch (Wazirabad to Okhla); **Yamuna Action Plan**; fish kills linked to low oxygen and effluents

topics.mains: Centre–State coordination (CAQM), crop-residue economics, public-health framing.

topics.news: Census marks languages under 10,000 speakers as "others"; Kurumba (oral, no script) of Kerala at risk; community is a PVTG.

rows: Notified by the President, **Art. 342**; National Commission for STs **Art. 338A**

Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups; from the **Dhebar Commission (1960–61)**'s "primitive tribal groups"; renamed in 2006; criteria: pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, declining or stagnant population, subsistence economy
**PM-JANMAN (2023)** targets PVTG habitations; **Forest Rights Act 2006** gives habitat rights to PVTGs
Five, including the **Kurumba** (others: Cholanaikayan, Kattunayakan, Koraga, Kadar)
**Eighth Schedule** (22 languages); **Art. 29** (protect culture), **350A** (mother-tongue teaching), **350B** (Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities); **Art. 51A(f)** composite culture
**SPPEL (2013)** for languages with under 10,000 speakers; **People's Linguistic Survey of India** found far more languages than the Census lists
UN International Decade of Indigenous Languages (2022–2032)

items.p: **Geography and livelihood:** **Attappady** (Palakkad), **Western Ghats**, Kerala's only tribal taluk; **Irula, Muduga, Kurumba**; shifting cultivation of **millets**; **Millet Village programme (2017)**; **sickle cell and anaemia** are health problems.

topics.mains: language is identity; Census classification rules shape which languages get support.

topics.t: MEGHALAYA — tribal land to a cement company
topics.news: Jaintia National Council wants the transfer of tribal land at Umkyrpong (East Jaintia Hills) for a cement and limestone project paused; valuation questioned.

rows: Carved out of Assam in **1972**; **Garo, Khasi, Jaintia** hills; matrilineal societies
**Three ADCs** (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo Hills); land is mostly communal or private, **not state-owned**; councils regulate land use and customary law
State law restricts transfer of tribal land to non-tribals
**MMDR Act 1957**; **NGT** banned rat-hole coal mining in **2014**; Supreme Court later vacated the ban; the Centre allowed scientific mining in 2025; limestone feeds the cement industry
**Shillong plateau**; **Cherrapunji/Mawsynram** among the wettest places; limestone and coal belts in the Jaintia Hills
**Lakadong turmeric** (high curcumin, Jaintia Hills), pineapple, oranges, areca nut, ginger

topics.mains: tribal land ownership vs industrial need; role of councils in consent.

topics.news: India's TB mortality down 38% since 2015 (global 35%); high treatment success; catastrophic costs; TB Mukt Bharat screening.

rows: Caused by **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, spreads through air; **MDR/XDR-TB** are drug-resistant forms
**RNTCP → National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)**; **Ni-kshay** portal; **Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana** (monthly nutrition support); **Ni-kshay Mitra** (community support)
India aimed for elimination by **2025** (missed); now aims for 2030; **WHO End TB Strategy**, **SDG 3.3**
WHO publishes the **Global TB Report** every year
**Public health is a State subject** (List II); **prevention of infectious diseases is Concurrent** (List III); **Art. 21, 47**

topics.mains: gains in mortality vs missed incidence targets; nutrition and catastrophic costs.

topics.news: ground static test of a modified third stage (PS3) at Sriharikota to bring the PSLV back on track.

rows: Founded **1969**; under the **Department of Space**; **NSIL** (commercial arm), **IN-SPACe** (2020, private-sector regulator), **Space Policy 2023**
"Workhorse"; four stages alternating **solid** and **liquid**; used for **Chandrayaan-1, Mangalyaan**, Astrosat and many foreign satellites; reaches **polar/sun-synchronous orbit**
Third stage, a **solid motor** with **HTPB** propellant; PSLV had **third-stage failures in May 2025 (C61) and Jan 2026 (C62)**, linked to a chamber-pressure drop; LVM3 (Gaganyaan) shares processes
**Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota** (Andhra Pradesh) — on the east coast, near the equator for a launch advantage; new spaceport at **Kulasekarapattinam** (Tamil Nadu)

topics.mains: reliability and quality control; private-sector manufacturing of stages.

topics.news: in-country inference for the API, first for one model, for firms with data-localisation needs.

ul: **Data residency** (where data sits) vs **local processing** (where the model computes).
**Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023**: data principal, **data fiduciary**, consent, **Data Protection Board**; cross-border transfer allowed except to restricted countries.
**Information Technology Act, 2000** (cyber law, intermediaries).
**Puttaswamy v. UoI (2017):** right to privacy is part of **Art. 21**.
**RBI 2018** rule: payment data must be stored in India.
**IndiaAI Mission (2024)** and MeitY's role; global frameworks such as the EU AI Act.

topics.mains: localisation vs free flow of data; sovereignty vs cost.

topics.news: IIT Madras swabbed Chennai Metro; distinct "transit biome"; antimicrobial-resistance genes widespread; global projects such as PathoMap and MetaSUB.

rows: Microbes stop responding to drugs; driven by overuse in humans, livestock and farming; **superbugs**
**Penicillin** discovered in 1928 (Fleming); **metagenomics** = reading all DNA in a sample; **microbiome**

**Chennai Declaration (2012)**, **NAP-AMR 2017**, **NAP-AMR 2.0 (2025–29)** launched in Nov 2025 with a **One Health** approach (human, animal, agriculture, environment); **Kerala's state plan (KARSAP, 2018)** was the first by a State
**Schedule H1** (prescription-only antibiotics), **Red Line campaign** (2016), **colistin banned in animal feed** (2019)
**ICMR AMR Surveillance Network**; **World AMR Awareness Week** (18–24 Nov)
**WHO Global Action Plan on AMR**; WHO list of priority pathogens
Chennai on the **Coromandel coast**; coastal humidity shapes its microbes
